baseline.title: Introducing LettuceDetect: A Lightweight Hallucination Detector for RAG Pipelines
baseline.body: Hallucinations remain a significant challenge in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, especially in specialized domains like medicine and law. Existing detection methods often face limitations such as restricted context window sizes, particularly with encoder-only models, and high inference costs due to reliance on large language models (LLMs). LettuceDetect is an open-source, encoder-based framework designed to flag hallucinated spans in LLM-generated answers without requiring an LLM. Built on ModernBERT, it can handle inputs up to 4,000 tokens and achieves 79.22% F1 on the RAGTruth benchmark. Licensed under MIT, LettuceDetect includes Python packages, pretrained models, and a Hugging Face demo. Community feedback is sought to explore its potential applications and ideas for real-time hallucination detection in local RAG setups.
